Gregory Thaumaturgus
GREG-or-ee thaw-ma-TUR-gus
proper noun
Greek Gregorios, “watchful,” with Thaumatourgos, “wonder-worker,” a third-century bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus.

Biblical Definition

Gregory, surnamed Thaumaturgus, “the wonder-worker,” was bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus in the third century, a pupil of Origen who turned from the law and philosophy to Christ. He composed a clear confession of the Trinity, the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost (2Co 13:14), which long served the church of Pontus as a rule of faith. He was a true missionary bishop, and it is said that he found his city with but a handful of believers and left it with but a handful of unbelievers, so mightily did the gospel spread under his labour, turning men from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God (Act 26:18). The dictionary honours Gregory as a missionary of fervent zeal and a faithful confessor of the Triune God. Yet his very surname, “the wonder-worker,” gathered to itself a crop of legendary marvels in the centuries after him, and his life was adorned with tales the sober reader must weigh against the Scripture. The dictionary honours the man and his real labour, while holding, with the apostle, that charity never faileth, but prophecies and tongues and the sign-gifts of the apostolic age shall cease (1Co 13:8), and that the church is built not on wonders but on the word.

Webster 1828 Definition

A third-century missionary bishop of Pontus and confessor of the Trinity, whose surname gathered later legends.

GREGORY THAUMATURGUS, “the wonder-worker,” bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus.

He flourished in the third century and was a pupil of Origen.

He composed a clear and early confession of the Trinity.

He was a fervent missionary who turned his region to Christ.

His surname gathered legendary marvels in the centuries after him.

Key Scripture

2Co 13:14 — "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen."

Rom 15:19 — "Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ."

1Co 13:8 — "Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away."

Act 26:18 — "To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me."

Modern Corruption

His missionary labour and Trinitarian confession are honoured, while the later cult of his wonders is weighed by the word.

expand to see more

What is honourable in Gregory is plain: a fervent missionary who carried the gospel through Pontus and confessed the Triune God in a creed that fed his people for generations. The dictionary honours such labour, by which men were turned from the power of Satan unto God, and gives thanks for the spread of the gospel under his hand.

The corruption to weigh is not in Gregory’s faith but in the legend that gathered about his name. “The wonder-worker” became a magnet for marvellous tales, and the cult of his miracles grew far beyond the sober record. The dictionary, holding the Reformed and cessationist rule, honours the man while it sifts the legend; for the church is built not upon signs and wonders but upon the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ Himself the chief corner stone. The extraordinary gifts that attended the founding of the church have ceased, and the marvels later heaped upon Gregory’s memory are no part of the rule of faith.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “watchful” and “wonder-worker,” the name marks a third-century missionary bishop of Pontus.

expand to see more

Gregory — Greek Gregorios, “watchful.”

Thaumaturgus — Greek Thaumatourgos, “wonder-worker.”

He was bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus in the third century.

He was a pupil of Origen and a confessor of the Trinity.

His surname gathered legendary marvels after his death.

Usage

"Like Gregory in Pontus, the missionary turns men from the power of Satan unto God."

"The church is built not upon signs and wonders but upon the word of God."

"Honour the faithful labourer, but weigh every later legend by the Scripture."
